title: Feature request: Product-specific customer tax exemptions for accurate wholesale and retail checkout
text: Shopify currently applies customer-level tax exemptions across all otherwise taxable purchases, without allowing merchants to restrict those exemptions to specific products or collections. This creates a significant tax compliance problem for small businesses operating both wholesale and retail sales through one Shopify store. The problem I operate a micro-scale flower farm and retail business in British Columbia, Canada. We sell flowers wholesale to professional florists alongside retail designed floral arrangements, books, pottery and, since we are relying on what we produce at the farm, we also sell fruit and other boutique products with various taxation levels. Some of our wholesale customers qualify for a BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) exemption when purchasing products for resale. However, those same customers occasionally purchase retail products for personal use, which are not eligible for that exemption. Currently, when a customer’s PST exemption is enabled in Shopify, it applies to all their otherwise PST-taxable purchases, regardless of whether the items are being purchased for resale or personal use. For example, a wholesale florist recently purchased a book from our retail boutique. Shopify correctly charged GST but removed PST because of the customer’s account-wide exemption even though the book was for personal use and needed to be taxed. The result is that Shopify’s existing tax settings cannot correctly accommodate a customer who makes both exempt and taxable purchases using the same account. The proposed solution Please introduce conditional, line-item customer tax exemptions , allowing merchants to specify which products or collections qualify for a particular customer’s tax exemption. When configuring a customer tax exemption, merchants should be able to choose whether it applies to: All otherwise eligible purchases, preserving the existing functionality. Specific products selected individually. Products selected through designated collections, as a convenient way to configure the underlying product-level rules. The actual tax calculation should occur at the individual line-item level, rather than relying solely on collection membership. For example, a BC PST resale exemption could apply to qualifying products purchased for resale from an approved wholesale collection, while purchases from our retail products would continue to be taxed normally. The exemption should apply only when both conditions are satisfied: The customer qualifies for the relevant tax exemption. The purchased product and its intended use qualify for that exemption under the applicable tax rules. Simply having access to a wholesale collection should not automatically make a customer or transaction tax-exempt. Ideally, Shopify would also allow merchants to use customer and product tags or metafields to configure these rules, making them easier to manage as businesses grow. Essential functionality The proposed system should: Correctly calculate taxes for mixed carts containing both exempt and taxable products. Support different tax treatments for the same customer account without requiring separate wholesale and retail accounts. Preserve existing product tax settings, collection tax overrides and other applicable tax exemptions. Allow customers to complete their own purchases through the normal online checkout. Calculate the correct tax amounts before payment, without requiring draft orders, manual adjustments or additional invoices. Record actual GST and PST amounts accurately in Shopify’s order records and tax reports. Be available on Shopify’s standard subscription plans, including Basic, rather than requiring Shopify Plus. The goal is not to create an alternative tax calculation system. It is to make Shopify’s existing customer exemption functionality more precise and compatible with businesses serving different types of customers and transactions. triage_reason: Lack of product-specific customer tax exemptions in Shopify creates wholesale compliance issues.

title: API 2026-10: created_at:> now skips orders from the rest of that second — check your incremental sync before upgrading
text: I upgraded an order sync integration to the 2026-10 API last week and found a breaking change in how created_at:> filtering works. If you run incremental syncs that checkpoint on a timestamp, this will affect you. What changed: from 2026-10, a > filter with no fractional seconds now starts at .999999 of that second. So created_at:>‘2026-09-15T12:00:02Z’ no longer returns an order created at 12:00:02.500. On 2026-07 and earlier the same filter would have returned it. Why it breaks incremental sync: order timestamps come back truncated to the second. If your job stores the last createdAt it saw and queries > that value on the next run, you used to get a small overlap of duplicates that you’d filter out by ID. After upgrading, you get a gap instead — anything created later in that same second, after your previous run, gets silently skipped. Shopify’s fix is straightforward: switch to >= and deduplicate on ID. But the gap is silent, so if you haven’t audited your sync since upgrading to 2026-10 you might not know it’s happening. The change only affects >, not >=, <, <=, date-only values, or values that already include fractional seconds. Apps still on 2026-07 or earlier are not affected. A couple of questions for anyone else who’s hit this: are you checkpointing on created_at or updated_at? And do you keep an overlap window as a safety buffer, or rely purely on the dedup? Curious whether bulk operation queries see the same behaviour — the docs don’t say explicitly. 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Breaking change in Shopify 2026-10 API timestamp filter behavior skips orders.
